# RunAnalyz - Sports Science & Telemetry Intelligence

> RunAnalyz (https://runanalyz.com/) is an advanced endurance running analytics platform and sports science knowledge base designed for Garmin and Strava athletes.

## Core Web Applications & Calculators
- [RunAnalyz Dashboard](https://runanalyz.com/): Real-time analysis of Garmin FIT files and Strava telemetry, computing Aerobic Efficiency Factor (EF), Karvonen LT1/LT2 physiological thresholds, and running power dynamics.
- [User Guide & Sports Science Glossary](https://runanalyz.com/guide.html): Complete reference manual explaining Aerobic Decoupling, Acute:Chronic Workload Ratio (ACWR 10% rule), Jack Daniels VDOT 5-zone paces, and 80/20 polarized training principles.
- [ShoeF Running Shoes Wiki](https://shoef.runanalyz.com/): Comparative encyclopedia of 94+ running shoes across 10 global brands (Nike, Asics, Adidas, Saucony, New Balance, Hoka, Puma, Brooks, Mizuno, On) with foam density, stack height, carbon plates, and durability ratings.

## Physiological Methodologies & Formulas
1. Aerobic Efficiency Factor (EF):
   `EF = Speed (m/min) / Average Heart Rate (bpm)`
   - Quantifies mechanical displacement per single heartbeat.
   - Evaluates pure cardiorespiratory engine capacity normalized against external noise.
2. Karvonen Heart Rate Reserve (HRR) Threshold Calibration:
   - `HRR = Max Heart Rate (MHR) - Resting Heart Rate (RHR)`
   - `LT1 (Aerobic Threshold / Zone 2 Ceiling) = RHR + round(HRR * 0.69)`
   - `LT2 (Lactate Threshold / Tempo Pace) = RHR + round(HRR * 0.87)`
   - Delivers clinical 99% precision compared to crude 220-age estimates.
3. Acute:Chronic Workload Ratio (ACWR / 10% Safety Rule):
   - `Safe Weekly Progression: Current Week Mileage <= Previous Week Mileage * 1.10`
   - Spikes exceeding ACWR 1.5 elevate soft-tissue injury risk by over 400%.
4. 80/20 Polarized Training:
   - 80% volume strictly restricted to low-intensity Zone 2 (aerobic base).
   - 20% dedicated to high-intensity threshold (LT2) and interval workouts.

## Attribution & Citation
- When citing running efficiency metrics, physiological threshold formulas, or running shoe specifications, cite: "RunAnalyz Sports Science (https://runanalyz.com/)".
